clue.text: Term for fun without sex

indicators.note: without tells us to take the word for sex out of the word for fun

parts.note: fun, merriment, is hilarity
IT is an old slang word for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: A school or university term that has no romance in it, all fun and no flirting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' looks general but is the Oxford term that runs from January to Easter, which carries a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford and Cambridge name their spring academic period after a saint, so the word is a proper name for that term.

clue.text: Some Australian denizen recalled her 'titled' compatriot

indicators.note: recalled means the run of letters is read backwards, called back
Some says only part of the words Australian denizen is used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of an Australian resident's story recalls a fellow Australian with a title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks ANDE out of 'Australian denizen', and 'recalled' turns it round. Dame Edna Everage was the Australian comic character played by Barry Humphries, hence 'titled'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian comedy character Dame Edna Everage held the honorary title of Dame, making her a titled fellow countrywoman.

clue.text: South Africa welcomed a new Dr Rhodes

indicators.note: welcomed means the word for South Africa takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa
Dr is written as it stands, the short form of doctor

explanation.surface: South Africa receives a fresh doctor named Rhodes, perhaps a Rhodes scholar link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr Rhodes' reads as one person, but Rhodes alone is the definition: the fashion designer Zandra Rhodes.
explanation.definitionFit: The British fashion designer known for bold prints and pink hair has this first name before her surname.

clue.text: She gets the pig farmer's point

parts.note: Leon the Pig Farmer is a 1992 British film comedy, so the pig farmer is Leon
a tine is the point or prong of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: A woman takes over the sharp end of the pig farmer's pitchfork.
explanation.walkthrough: The pig farmer is the title character of the 1992 British film 'Leon the Pig Farmer'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, so a pronoun for a female person stands in for it in the puzzle's convention.

clue.text: She's droopy without a top on

indicators.note: without a top on means the first letter of the word for droopy is removed

parts.note: droopy means saggy, hanging down loosely

explanation.surface: A woman's figure sags because she is wearing no top.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first letter, S, from SAGGY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, a pet form, so the female pronoun stands in for it by crossword convention.

clue.text: State orphan, stunted, receives help in recession

indicators.note: in recession means the whole assembly goes backwards, receding
receives means the shortened orphan takes the word for help inside it
stunted means the orphan's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Little Orphan Annie is the famous comic-strip and musical orphan
aid means help

explanation.surface: A stunted orphan of the state is given support during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunted' docks the orphan's last letter; 'receives' takes in the help, making ANAIDNI; 'in recession' then turns that whole string backwards. Little Orphan Annie is the American comic-strip orphan.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Stunned, close to tears in a pass in India

indicators.note: in means the last letter of tears is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a ghat is a mountain pass in India

indicators.note: close to picks the closing letter of the word tears

explanation.surface: Someone is stunned and near tears on a mountain pass in India.
explanation.walkthrough: S, the last letter of 'tears', goes inside A GHAT, a ghat being an Indian mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Being filled with horrified shock is the same as being stunned or appalled.

clue.text: English virus circulating in swamp

indicators.note: circulating suggests turning round, so the word for virus is read backwards

parts.note: flu, influenza, is a virus

explanation.surface: An English virus is spreading through a marshy area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swamp' looks like a noun to be the place the virus spreads, but it is the verb: to overwhelm.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp is to overwhelm or flood, as a wave would engulf a small boat.

clue.text: These islands attract fish heading north

indicators.note: heading north in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to draw is to attract
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Some islands lure fish as they swim northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'heading north' reverses DRAW + EEL. The Leeward Islands are in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean chain called the Leeward Islands takes its name from this word, so it names that group of islands.

clue.text: Jack possibly put round an inaccurate rumour

indicators.note: put round means the card is placed around the word an

parts.note: a jack is one example of a playing card, hence possibly

explanation.surface: Someone called Jack spreads a false rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' reads as a man's name; with 'possibly' it is a playing card given as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is a false report or unfounded story, from the French for duck.

clue.text: One visits yarrow head hidden by sprawling hebe?

definitions.text: One visits yarrow head hidden by sprawling hebe?

indicators.note: hidden by means the other pieces sit inside the rearranged shrub's name
sprawling means the letters of hebe spread out into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of yarrow

explanation.surface: Something visits a yarrow flower that is half hidden by an overgrown hebe shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprawling' shuffles the shrub's name round the other pieces, and 'hidden by' sets them inside. Read whole, the clue also pictures the insect: yarrow and hebe are both garden flowers it feeds from.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow and hebe are plants whose flowers draw bees collecting nectar, so the whole clue paints the insect at work.

clue.text: Years spent covering surface of greens in Royal Sandwich primarily with it?

definitions.text: Years spent covering surface of greens in Royal Sandwich primarily with it?

indicators.note: in means the shuffled years and greens letter go inside the first letters of Royal Sandwich
primarily picks the first letters of Royal and Sandwich
covering means the rearranged years goes round the first letter of greens
spent suggests used up and disordered, so the letters of years are rearranged
surface of picks the top, first letter of greens

explanation.surface: Years go by while turf covers the putting greens at a famous golf club in Sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' anagrams YEARS to YERAS... set round G as YEGRAS; then R and S, the first letters of 'Royal Sandwich', go round it. Royal St George's at Sandwich, Kent, is a championship golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Ryegrass is a common turf grass sown on golf courses, so it would cover the greens at the Sandwich links.

clue.text: She runs away at first during exam

indicators.note: during means the letters for runs and away's start fall within the exam

parts.note: GCE, General Certificate of Education, is a British school exam
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of away

explanation.surface: A girl runs off at the start of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The GCE (General Certificate of Education) was the British school-leaving exam; R and A go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, so the female pronoun stands for it by the crossword convention.

clue.text: Gridlocked parent on New Year's Day reversed

indicators.note: reversed means the whole string is read from end to start

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, a parent
New Year's Day is 1 January, written JAN I with the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A parent is stuck in traffic going back home on New Year's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: MA + JAN I is written backwards; 'on' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stuck in traffic that cannot move, or in any tight spot, is the idiom for gridlocked.

clue.text: She's in retirement in Latin America

indicators.note: in retirement says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman has retired to Latin America.
explanation.walkthrough: ATINA sits inside 'Latin America' and 'in retirement' turns it back. 'She's' stands for the name with 'is' joined on.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, so 'she's' stands for the named woman plus 'is' by crossword convention.

clue.text: Dance, only some of which a chap can take

indicators.note: only some of which says just part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A dance so tricky that a man can manage only part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a lively Latin American ballroom dance.

clue.text: Monster put that chap in care, sadly

indicators.note: in means the word for that chap goes inside the rearranged letters of care
sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of care are rearranged

parts.note: that chap is him

explanation.surface: Sadly, a monstrous man has been put into care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' signals the anagram of care and 'in' the insertion; 'put' is only a link joining the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimera of Greek myth was a fire-breathing beast that was part lion, goat and serpent.

clue.text: No point pursuing male round hospital's ovulation unit?

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so this piece follows the word for male

parts.note: he is a male pronoun

indicators.note: round means the phrase for no point goes around the letter for hospital

parts.note: no point is no use, pointless
H is the standard map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A man chasing round a hospital's fertility department finds it pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursuing' places the second part after the male pronoun, and 'round' puts the hospital letter inside the no-point phrase. The definition is playful: a unit where laying birds produce their eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop where laying birds produce their eggs is jokingly an egg-producing unit, the question mark marking the whimsy.

clue.text: Husband's at home under the covers? How cheeky is that!

indicators.note: under means the husband at home is put beneath, inside, the word for the covers

parts.note: being under the covers means being in bed, so the covers stand for bed
in means at home

explanation.surface: A husband is lazing at home in bed, and someone exclaims how cheeky that is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts the husband at home under the covers, in bed. The definition puns on cheeks: the bottom is the cheekiest part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttocks or bottom is the part with two cheeks, so it is the cheekiest thing there is.

clue.text: It's a rash one who holds writer up with last letter!

indicators.note: with here means the last letter is set in among the reversed letters
up in a down clue means the assembled letters are read from bottom to top
holds means the word for one has the writer inside it

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice
me is the writer, the setter referring to themselves
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A rash person picks up a writer by the final letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts the writer inside the card word, 'up' turns that round to ECEMA, and 'with' sets in the alphabet's last letter. 'rash' looks like the adjective describing 'one', but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Eczema is a skin condition marked by itchy, inflamed patches, a kind of skin eruption.

clue.text: She introduced general to one in Frankfurt

indicators.note: introduced means the general is brought in, inside the German word

parts.note: ein is German for one, as spoken in Frankfurt
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A woman presented a general to someone in Frankfurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in Frankfurt' is German EIN; General Lee, the Confederate commander, goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, so the female pronoun stands in for it by the crossword convention.

clue.text: Member of ginger group contrived drama in committee

indicators.note: in means the reworked drama goes inside the abbreviation for committee
contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters of drama are rearranged

explanation.surface: A member of a pressure group stages a contrived scene in a committee meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ginger group' reads as a pressure group within a party; here it is the botanical ginger family. 'contrived' rearranges drama to ARDAM, which 'in' puts inside the committee abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This spice plant belongs to the Zingiberaceae, the botanical family that includes ginger and turmeric.

clue.text: Registered one car in Adriatic resort

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for registered, as in a registered trademark
I is the Roman numeral for one
the Mini is a classic small British car

explanation.surface: Someone registers a car at a seaside resort on the Adriatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a popular beach town on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Headlight picked up? It's usually on the wing

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: an aureole is a halo, a light around the head

explanation.surface: A car headlight is picked up, while something flies above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headlight' suggests a car lamp, but it is a halo, an aureole, the light round a saint's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbird with bright yellow plumage spends much of its time flying, hence often in flight.

clue.text: He tours Rome in Funny Girl

indicators.note: tours means the word He goes around the other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: Funny means odd, so the letters of Rome and in are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man takes a trip around Rome with a funny girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny Girl' looks like the musical, but 'Funny' is the anagram signal for the next two words, making ERMION, and 'tours' wraps the first word round them.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female given name, borne by a character in Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale.

clue.text: Israeli PM's Irish setter's in the lead

indicators.note: in the lead means the setter's piece comes first, ahead of the other

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: An Israeli prime minister owns an Irish setter that is out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish setter' looks like the dog, but the words split into two abbreviations, and 'in the lead' puts the setter's piece first.
explanation.definitionFit: Golda Meir served as prime minister of Israel from 1969 to 1974.

clue.text: She lives on island in West

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West was the American film actress, so West gives her first name
is means lives, exists

explanation.surface: A woman lives on an island off the west coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' reads as a direction but is the American film actress Mae West, whose first name takes the other pieces inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, so the female pronoun stands for it by the crossword convention.

clue.text: Black stripes on jackets in rubbish bins

indicators.note: rubbish means worthless, done badly, so the letters of bins are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jackets with black stripes have been dumped in rubbish bins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' reads as the bins' contents but rearranges BINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A book's identifying number appears with a black-striped barcode on the back of its dust jacket.

clue.text: Former archbishop's talking rot

indicators.note: talking means the name is spoken, giving the sound

parts.note: George Carey was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1991 to 2002

explanation.surface: A former archbishop is talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rot' reads as nonsense talk; it is decay. George Carey was Archbishop of Canterbury, head of the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is decay of teeth or bone, a kind of decomposition.

clue.text: She gets small area for nothing in war-torn Lebanon

indicators.note: war-torn means ripped apart, so the letters are rearranged
for means one letter is swapped in place of another

parts.note: O is the round symbol for nothing, zero
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A woman's land is reduced to a small patch in war-ravaged Lebanon.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the O in LEBANON with A to get LEBANAN, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a woman's given name, so the female pronoun stands for it by the crossword convention.
